title: CDIF progress: new profiles and roadmap coming soon!
content:
Developments on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) have been moving rapidly since the release of version 1.1 and the launch of the CDIF4EOSC project in June 2026. Work has been focused on both immediate- and longer-term objectives, in a variety of areas. Chief among these are the new profiles under development, a long-running process which is now bearing fruit. Efforts to support the further development of cross-domain metadata models at W3C are on-going, and there are developments in terms of tools, maintenance, and training. The recent workshop ‘Optimising Metadata Structures for Alignments with Standard Models at the Point of Use’ at the Leibniz Foundation’s Schloss Dagstuhl in Wadern, Germany saw many of these activities come to a head.

New Profiles: Provenance, Access Rights and DCAT-Syntax for Core and Discovery Profiles

title: From FAIR to combinable and meaningful data: the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF)
content:
How can data from different fields be combined and understood by both people and machines, across different technical and scientific ecosystems?

To mark the 10th anniversary of the CODATA-RDA Schools of Research Data Science, CODATA and the GO FAIR Foundation (GFF) organised a session on this question in Trieste on 16 November 2026.

Here are the slides on the FAIR principles and FAIR Implementation Profiles, presented by Dario Bijker (GFF).

Here are the slides on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) presented by Nina Grau (CODATA).

Sharing data is no longer enough. There is an increasing need to combine data from different disciplines and across different systems. This is only possible when data is accompanied by clear and consistent information about what it is and what it contains: its metadata. Yet each community describes its data in its own way.
